quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Your body can only remove alcohol through:
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: For the most protection, choose a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards for maximum protection. Helmets should fit snugly all the way around.

questions.question: The front brake is:

options.text: Only for use if the rear brake fails.

questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used correctly. It is more powerful than the rear brake and provides about three-fourths of your total stopping power.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen frequently, so do not worry about them.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds under 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can be fatal.

questions.question: If stopping your motorcycle will take longer than usual, you should:
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when riding on slippery surfaces. Give yourself more space to stop if stopping takes longer than usual.

questions.question: Gloves can:

options.text: Make motorcycle control difficult and should be avoided.
Improve your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Improve your grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves give you a better grip on your handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Wearing a helmet:

options.text: Increases the risk of neck injury.
Reduces the risk of neck injury.
Improves your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Improves your chances of surviving a crash.
questions.explanation: A helmet reduces the risk of head and neck injuries and is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash. DOT-approved helmets let you see to the sides as much as needed for safe riding.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Assume everything on your motorcycle will work.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: A small problem on a motorcycle can be more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: The proper riding position is when you:

options.text: Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the handlebars.
Sit as far back as possible and stretch to reach the handlebars.
Lean over the bike so your arms hold you up.
Keep your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Sit forward so your arms are slightly bent when you hold the handlebars. This makes it easy to reach and operate the controls comfortably.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: Before you get on a motorcycle, which of these do you NOT need to check?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire tread and air pressure, oil and fluid levels, lights, and signals.

questions.question: What kind of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride a motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Tell them to use quiet roads.

questions.explanation: Never let someone ride if they have had too much to drink. Stop them from riding by taking their keys if needed. Help them find another way to get home.

questions.question: When you adjust your rearview mirror, what should you be able to see?

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
Only the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the lane next to you as possible. The road behind and beside you is more important than seeing your arm or shoulder.

questions.question: When you check your brakes before riding, what should you make sure of?

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes cause some friction with steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, test each brake lever by itself. Make sure each one feels firm and stops the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: What kind of jacket protects you best when riding?

options.text: One that leaves your arms exposed.
One that should not be worn in warm weather.

questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket made of leather for protection. Your clothes should fit snug enough to not flap in the wind, but not so tight you cannot move. Wear protective gear even in hot weather because many riding jackets prevent overheating.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be which of the following?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are usually rectangular and white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: If one of your tires goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Gently apply the brake of the good tire.
Speed up to leave the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake of the good tire.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and ride straight as you slow down. If you need to brake, slowly apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: When choosing clothes for riding, which is NOT a good choice?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely.
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles.
A baseball cap to cover your hair.

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair.
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a jacket and long pants made of strong material, boots or shoes that are high and sturdy to cover your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: From the front or back, a motorcycle's size is _______ a car's.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's outline is much smaller than a car's. This makes it easy for other drivers to miss you on the road.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead.
Do not use your rearview mirrors to watch traffic behind you.
Look for chances to squeeze through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Stay back from the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if that vehicle backs up or if another vehicle comes too fast from behind.

questions.question: What material works best for riding gloves?
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another strong material to protect your hands.

questions.question: How often should you inspect your motorcycle before riding?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride to prevent safety problems. Small issues on a motorcycle are more dangerous than on a car.

questions.question: What should you do with your headlight during the day?

options.text: Turn it on only when it is cloudy.
Use it only if you think it helps.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to see you.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after drinking one alcoholic drink, can you ride safely?

options.text: No, you cannot be arrested for drinking and driving.
Yes, the alcohol will not affect your riding skills.
No, alcohol effects may still remain.
Yes, as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, alcohol effects may still remain.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink of alcohol per hour. But alcohol can still build up in your system and affect your ability to ride safely.
